guide.title: Bretwood North Course: Golf in Keene, New Hampshire
guide.intro: Every other guide in this fifty-state set is anchored on the highest-ranked entry carrying Golf Digest's own "Public" label on that state's Best in State 2025-'26 ranking. New Hampshire is one of four states in the set where that cannot be done, and it is the state where the negative is proved hardest. The New Hampshire ranking has exactly five entries — 1 Baker Hill Golf Club (Newbury), 2 The Golf Club of New England (Stratham), 3 Lake Winnipesaukee Golf Club (New Durham), 4 Manchester Country Club (Bedford), 5 Lake Sunapee Country Club (New London) — and every one of the five is labelled "Private." The word "Public" does not occur anywhere in the ranking page's 432 KB body, not as a label and not as anything else, and it does not occur in any of six archived captures of the same page reaching back to March 2025. All five clubs additionally state a member-or-member's-guest gate in their own words on their own sites. With no publicly accessible entry at any rank to anchor on, this guide uses the set's stated fallback instead: the publicly accessible course in the state with the strongest verifiable competitive record. That is the North Course at Bretwood Golf Course, 365 East Surry Rd, Keene, in Cheshire County — host of 19 New Hampshire Open Championships, more than any other course in that championship's history. It is a fallback anchor and carries no ranking of its own. The section below sets out how the negative was proved, in enough detail that a reader can go and check it.

sections.heading: Getting there
sections.body: Bretwood Golf Course is at 365 East Surry Rd, Keene, NH 03431; the number on every page of its own site is 603.352.7626. The US Census geocoder matches that address as 365 E SURRY RD, KEENE, NH, 03431 at -72.304944931935, 42.980623418626, and returns Cheshire County, Keene city, Census Tract 9710; the course polygon's own centroid geocodes to the same county, the same place and the same tract. Manchester–Boston Regional Airport (MHT) is the airport with scheduled airline service a traveller flies into: a road-routing engine returns 61.1 miles from the course to the airport. Bradley International (BDL), Windsor Locks, Connecticut, routes at 85.8 road miles, and Boston Logan International (BOS) at 92.8. The MHT route was described in research as running essentially the length of NH Route 101 — East Surry Road and Court Street into Keene, then NH 101 east through Marlboro Street, Peterborough, Wilton Road and the Gibbons Highway, then NH Route 3A (Brown Avenue) and Airport Road — but that description was not re-derived turn by turn, so it is set down here as reported rather than as verified; the mileages were. Keene has its own field, Dillant-Hopkins Airport (EEN), whose service class was not established, which is why MHT is the airport this guide names. One thing to get right before you type anything: the operator's domain is bretwoodgc.com. The https form of bretwoodgolf.com is a Squarespace parking page — 1,100 bytes, titled "Coming Soon," reading "We're under construction," with zero occurrences of "Bretwood" or "Keene" in it. The http form of that same domain redirects to the real site, so testing the wrong one of the two gives the wrong answer.

sections.heading: A different rule for this state
sections.body:
Golf Digest publishes a Best in State ranking for New Hampshire at golfdigest.com/courses/guides/new-hampshire-best-golf-courses-rankings, and the page dates its own edition in its own sentence: "Below you'll find our 2025-'26 ranking of the Best Golf Courses in New Hampshire." The host discriminates on request headers and refuses most machine requests, but a browser-shaped header profile returns HTTP 200 and a body of about 432,600 bytes titled "The best golf courses in New Hampshire | Golf Courses | GolfDigest.com," terminating cleanly in a closing script, body and html tag rather than truncated, and containing Baker Hill nine times, Golf Club of New England nine, Lake Winnipesaukee eight, Lake Sunapee ten and Manchester Country Club five. That is a content test, not a status test: it is the ranking, not a not-found shell.

The list is five entries long and the access labels were read from inside each entry's own header block rather than by position on the page, because this ranking renders its countdown bottom-up — in document order the blocks run 5, 4, 3, 2, 1, by Golf Digest's own internal course ids 7396, 7400, 12625, 19656, 20099. The page carries five header blocks, five title elements and five label elements: the three counts match exactly, so no entry is unlabelled and no entry can be silently inheriting a neighbour's label. Read that way the five are 1 Baker Hill Golf Club, Newbury, rated 4.2 by 9 panelists, previous rank 1, labelled Private; 2 The Golf Club of New England, Stratham, 4.1 from 7 panelists, previous rank 2, Private; 3 Lake Winnipesaukee Golf Club, New Durham, 3.9 from 5 panelists, previous rank 3, Private; 4 Manchester Country Club, Bedford, 3.9 from 5 panelists, previous rank 5, Private; 5 Lake Sunapee Country Club, New London, 3.1 from 5 panelists, previously unranked, Private. The string "Public" occurs zero times in the whole document. The HTML entity for a double quote also occurs zero times, which matters because it is how an HTML-escaped record set would show itself: there is no hidden payload carrying entries the rendered list does not show. Five entries is the whole list.

The negative holds over time, not just on one fetch. The Internet Archive's index returns eight successful captures of this page, and six of them were downloaded and parsed independently: 24 March 2025, 17 June 2025, 5 August 2025, 8 October 2025, 18 February 2026 and 20 May 2026. Three of those measure 433,357, 460,354 and 486,224 bytes and are provably three different snapshots rather than one address fetched three ways — three different archive digests, three different MD5 hashes, and no redirect collapsing any pair onto another. Every one of the six shows five blocks, five rubrics, five titles, five Private labels and zero occurrences of "Public." The March 2025 capture is not even the same edition: it lacks the 2025-'26 string, it renders top-down, and it seats Portsmouth Country Club at rank 4 — and it too is all Private. Across seven independent views spanning March 2025 to the present edition, this ranking has never carried a "Public" label at any rank.

The second proof shares no artefact with the first. Each club's own site was reached through Golf Digest's own outbound link and confirmed by its footer street address before anything was quoted, and each states its gate in its own words. Baker Hill Golf Club, 101 Baker Hill Road, Newbury: "What is the guest policy? Guests must play with a member. With the exception of visiting family members, a guest may play a maximum of six days per season," and "Baker Hill hosts 2-3 charity events during the season." The Golf Club of New England, 167 Winnicutt Road, Stratham: the club is run "for the enjoyment of our members, their families, and guests," and its entire public site is Home, History, Guest Info, The Course, Careers and Contact plus a Member Login — no rate card, no tee-time page, no public booking path. Lake Winnipesaukee Golf Club, One Lake Winnipesaukee Drive, New Durham: "Welcome to the Lake Winnipesaukee Golf Club, a private club and friendly gathering place maintained for the enjoyment of the members, their families, and their guests," under a homepage strapline reading "A Private Members' Golf Club." Manchester Country Club, 180 South River Road, Bedford: "Golfing guests of members are encouraged to use the bag drop located at the clubhouse entrance," and "The main lot is reserved for members and their guests"; the club's own homepage cites its awards as Best Golf Course (Private) from NH Magazine and the 2025 BOB Award from NH Business Review for Best Private Golf Course. Lake Sunapee Country Club, 289 Country Club Lane, New London, whose page title reads "Private Golf Course": "Is the course private? Yes. Access to the golf course is provided via club membership," and "Non-member guests may play the course a total of two times per month." The same FAQ adds "Is the course available for use by daily fee users? Reciprocal play is available on a limited basis" — that is reciprocal play for members of other clubs, not a path for an unaffiliated traveller, so the gate stands.

With no publicly accessible entry at any rank, this guide falls back to the criterion the set reserves for exactly this case: the publicly accessible course with the strongest verifiable competitive record. That is the North Course at Bretwood.

sections.heading: The alternative that loses, and why it loses
sections.body:
New Hampshire's most famous golf resort is not New Hampshire's course under this criterion, and the reason is worth stating because it is not the reason a reader would guess. The Mount Washington Course at Omni Mount Washington Resort & Spa, in Bretton Woods, Carroll County, was tested for access rather than assumed to be gated, and the test came out in favour of access. The resort's own golf FAQ asks and answers it directly: "Do you have to be a guest staying at Omni Mount Washington Resort & Spa to play on the golf courses? No, the public is welcome although resort guests have priority for booking tee times," and adds that "Golf is available for guests and the Bretton Woods public by visiting the tee time website or by calling the clubhouse at 603-278-4653." That is access, not a gate, and the course itself is a serious one: the resort states that it "was designed by legendary Scottish Architect Donald Ross and was completed in 1915," that it is a par 72 of 7,004 yards, and that it "Reopened on August 1, 2008" after a restoration to Ross's original plans by Brian Silva. Its season, in the resort's words, is "open seasonally from May - October, pending weather."

It loses on record, and only on record. The resort's own course page states that the course "has hosted four New Hampshire Opens and the prestigious New England Open Championship in September 2010," and that figure checks out independently against the championship's venue-by-year history: the Mount Washington Hotel hosted in 1977, 1978, 1979 and 1980. Four against Bretwood's nineteen is the whole of the comparison. Two other things a reader should know about it. First, no green fee is published for it and none is printed here: the page headed "Golf Rates And Fees" carries a single table, "Practice Range & Rental Rates," whose two columns are "Adult 18+" and "Junior/Teen Under 17" — not guest and non-guest — listing range balls at $10, rental clubs at $85 adult and $75 junior for 18 holes and $65 and $55 for 9, driving-range rental clubs at $15, and practice-range season memberships at $475 family, $375 couple and $300 single. The words "green fee" and "non-guest" appear nowhere on it, and the only occurrence of 2026 on the page is the footer copyright line, so there is no rate and no dated qualifier to publish. Second, its green-fee-bearing booking engine renders in the browser rather than on the server, so no figure could be read out of it either.

One more correction belongs here, because an earlier reading of this state got it wrong. North Conway Country Club, the other course tied on 11 New Hampshire Opens, is not a members' club with limited outside play. It is publicly accessible: its own navigation carries Rates, Tee Times and Golf Shop, its homepage advertises a public midweek 18-hole special, and membership is offered as an option rather than as a gate. It loses to Bretwood the same way the Omni does — 11 hostings against 19 — and for no other reason.

sections.heading: The North Course
sections.body:
Bretwood's own staff list names its "Course Architects — Geoffrey Cornish, Hugh Barrett," with John Pawlak as Director of Golf and PGA Professional and Jonas Maynard as Superintendent. The operator publishes no opening year for either course anywhere on its site, and none is asserted here; third-party chronologies exist but were not established from a first-party source. The published North Course scorecard runs four sets of tees: Gold 3,680 out and 3,294 in for 6,974 yards, par 37 and 35 for 72, rated 73.9 with a slope of 132; Blue 71.4/129; White 68.9/121; Red 68.8/116. In the operator's own description the setting is the river: "Our lush, superbly maintained 36 holes play along the picturesque Ashuelot River, which lazily meanders its way through the two courses," with "Four sets of tees, large Penncross bentgrass greens protected by strategic bunkering and mounds, generous and gently rolling fairways, many elevation changes, lots of water and the ever-present wind."

The record is the New Hampshire Open Championship, the state open, played since 1932 and run by New Hampshire Golf. Previewing the 2025 edition — played June 19-21, 2025 on the North Course — the state association wrote that "this year marks the 19th time Bretwood has hosted the prestigious championship—more than any other course in the event's history." That count was not taken on trust. It was re-derived from the championship's own venue-by-year table, which gives Bretwood 18 solo hostings — 1981, then 1990 through 2002, then 2004, 2006, 2023 and 2025 — plus the 2019 championship, whose venue is recorded as Bretwood Golf Club and Keene Country Club together. Eighteen plus the co-hosting is nineteen, and the association's figure and the table agree exactly. The runners-up on that record are Manchester Country Club and North Conway Country Club at 11 each, Portsmouth Country Club and Nashua Country Club at 7, Keene Country Club at 5 solo hostings (6 counting the shared 2019), and Atkinson Resort & Country Club and the Mount Washington Hotel at 4.

The state association describes the championship layout as "a 6,900-yard layout known for its wide fairways, challenging greens, and picturesque setting along the Ashuelot River" where "the North Course rewards strategic shot-making and precision, particularly on its stretch of risk-reward par 5s and demanding par 3s," and quotes the verdict that "Bretwood's North Course is one of the most respected championship venues in New Hampshire. It's always in fantastic condition and presents a great balance of scoring opportunities and demanding holes." The 2026 championship was not at Bretwood: the state association's own newsroom carries "A Championship Tradition Continues: Nashua CC Poised to Host 92nd NH Open," dated 17 June 2026, so the multi-day tournament closure that affects some championship venues does not apply to Bretwood in 2026. The operator claims no national ranking position, no conservation designation, no historic-register listing and no Audubon certification, and this guide claims none on its behalf.

sections.heading: Playing Bretwood
sections.body:
Bretwood is public on the operator's own terms and on a booking system that was driven rather than described. Its course-information page calls it a "36-hole public golf course (two 18 hole courses)"; its homepage invites you to play "two of the finest, most challenging and best maintained public golf courses in the Northeast"; and its tee-times page states that "Bretwood is a public 36-hole golf course and we are pleased to invite golfers to join us 7 days a week," that "Online tee time management is available for all guests," that "Active members can make tee time 14 days out. Non-members have 5 days," and that "Non-members can use the general public online tee time portal to book new tee times." Membership here is a season pass and not a right of entry: the membership page describes it as entitling you to unlimited rounds "throughout the course of a season (April thru November) – it's like a 'season pass' for golf," and its stated golfing advantage is booking, not access — "Members can also reserve weekend/holiday tee times two weeks in advance – one week earlier than non-members."

The general-public link on that page resolves to Bretwood's own Club Caddie portal, separate from the members' login. An unauthenticated request to it was issued a session id with no account and no sign-in, and the tee sheet was then requested for four dates spread across the calendar — 6 September 2026, 9 September 2026, 20 October 2026 and 15 December 2026. All four returned HTTP 200 and a page of about 90,000 bytes headed with the course's own identity, "Bretwood Golf Course — 365 East Surry Rd, New Hampshire, Keene, 03431 - United States," carrying Players, Holes, Time, Price and Rate Type filters, the rate options Any, Morning Rates, Afternoon Rates and Evening Rates, and a Login/Register control — an account can be created at the point of booking. There is no membership gate and no booking class. The limit of that test is worth stating plainly: the slot inventory itself is drawn in the browser, so the server's response carries no clock times and no prices at all, and no specific bookable tee time could be read out of it. What the test establishes is that the portal is Bretwood's own, is reachable without an account, and offers a non-member path; what it does not establish is any particular time.

The fees are the operator's own and carry the operator's own date. The rate page is titled "Rates for 2026" and states: "Rates listed here are current as of January 1, 2026. If a discrepancy exists, then the published rates in the Bretwood Golf Shop will take precedence over those found on this site." One card covers both 18-hole courses. From opening day through Thursday May 31, 2026: 9 holes $34 Monday to Thursday and $38 Friday, weekend and holiday; 18 holes $52 and $58; 36 holes Monday to Thursday $105 including cart. For the summer season after June 1, 2026: 9 holes $36 and $40 (the $40 rate before 7:00 am and after 11:00 am); 18 holes $54 and $60; 36 holes Monday to Thursday $110 including cart, non holiday. A motorised cart is $24 for two riders over 9 holes ($12.00 per person) or $15 for one rider, and $40.00 for two riders over 18 ($20.00 per person) or $25 for one; the card notes that "2026 members can purchase a '10 play cart card' at $180.00," that a driver's licence is required for rental, and that "Carts may not be rented or operated by junior golfers under 18 years old." A pull cart is $4 for 9 holes and $8 for 18, club rental $10 and $20, and a range bucket $6 for one token (36 balls) or $12 for two (72 balls). Membership, dated the same way, runs $1450 adult and $875 student or young adult aged 18 to 23 as of 4/1/2026; the junior 5 to 11 rate is $375, and the junior 12 to 17 row is published in the table without a price.

The season is published as a month range and nothing finer. The operator writes "Open every day from April until mid-November (weather permitting)" and, on the membership page, "a season (April thru November)," and the homepage adds that online tee times open "beginning April 1, Wednesday," with carts and tee times starting at 5:30 am on weekends and holidays and 6:00 am Monday through Friday. No exact opening or closing date is published anywhere on the site — there is no season-dates page, no news page and no course-status page — so this guide states the range and does not invent the dates. Nor is there a hidden closure notice: the raw HTML of the home, rates, tee-times and course-information pages contains no occurrence of aeration, renovation or flood at all, and the only closure wording in real page text is a note about the golf shop and range rather than the course — "Tokens can be used after shop hours. Closed early Monday night for maintenance." Every HTML comment on all four pages was extracted and read: they are layout markers for the masthead, the content wrapper and the page's own scripts, and nothing else, so there is no disabled notice for a tag-strip to resurrect. The site's events calendar returns zero events for a window bounded at both ends in 2026 and for one bounded across 2024 to 2026 alike, which means the calendar is unused rather than empty, and it is therefore evidence of nothing in either direction.

sections.heading: The South Course
sections.body:
The second course to play is Bretwood's South Course, on the same property at 0.0 road miles, sharing the clubhouse, the golf shop, the rate card, the season statement and the booking portal with the North. It is a full, separate 18 rather than a practice loop, and that was established three independent ways: the operator's own words, "36-hole public golf course (two 18 hole courses)"; the mapped course object's tags, which record two 18-hole layouts named North and South at par 72 each; and the operator's own scorecard page, which publishes two complete 18-hole cards. The South card reads Gold 3,374 out and 3,578 in for 6,952 yards, par 36 and 36 for 72, rated 73.5 with a slope of 132; Blue 70.7/125; White 67.7/117; Red 69.1/114. It carries its own local rules — "Out of Bounds: Behind green #12; Left of fairway #13" — and marks lateral water hazards along the Ashuelot River at holes 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 10, 11, 14 and 17. The rate card prices the pair as one day's golf at $105 Monday to Thursday before June 1, 2026 and $110 after, cart included.

Choosing a course on the same property was not a shortcut. Every mapped golf course within 60 kilometres of Bretwood was swept — 42 objects, of which seven turned out to be individual hole and tee markers inside another course's grounds and three more were practice centres rather than rounds of golf. The second-nearest object in that sweep, at 5.55 kilometres, carried no name, no website and no address at all; rather than skip it, it was identified by geocoding Keene Country Club's published address at 755 West Hill Rd, which lands 0.48 kilometres from the polygon's centre, on the same property. Keene Country Club fails on its own words — "a member-owned, full service private country club," whose "Golfing enthusiasts and their guests play our challenging, well-maintained, vintage Wayne Stiles course" — with no green fee and no public tee sheet, under a page title reading "Private Country Club in Keene, NH." It is 6.3 road miles from Bretwood. The nearest off-property course after that is Pine Grove Springs in Spofford at 10.9 road miles, whose domain does not resolve in DNS at all, so its access could not be established from its own words and it is not proposed here. Hooper Golf Course in Walpole, 15.8 road miles, does have a live site and is public — its own page title reads "Hooper Golf Course, Walpole, NH - Public 9 Hole Golf Course," and the stated benefit on its membership page is "exclusive access to tee times 2 weeks in advance (1 week for nonmembers)," which means non-members book. Both of the state's ranked courses that fall inside the sweep, Baker Hill at rank 1 and Lake Sunapee at rank 5, are farther away than all of these and private besides.

sections.heading: Keene, and where the weekend happens
sections.body:
Bretwood has a snack bar with beer and wine service, on-course snack shacks at the turn on both courses, a clubhouse with a large banquet area, a fully stocked golf shop, a driving range with grass tees in season, chipping and putting facilities, a large cart fleet and on-course restrooms — but no lodging. The weekend therefore happens in Keene, 3.8 to 4.1 road miles from the course along East Surry Road and Court Street.

The Burrell House Inn, 112 Washington Street, Keene, +1 (413) 239-9011, is 3.8 road miles from Bretwood and 0.3 road miles from Central Square. It describes itself as "a historic New England family-owned boutique hotel that's newly renovated with modern amenities" with "9 beautifully restored rooms," each carrying "fresh quality cotton linens, a full private bath, wi-fi, smart TV with cable, temperature control, microwave, mini-fridge, single coffee maker, coded entry, private parking, and complimentary soap, shampoo, and coffee." It does not serve breakfast and says so itself, pointing guests to the town's restaurants and cafés instead. The Chesterfield Inn, 20 Cross Road, West Chesterfield, (603) 256-3211, is the other option at 16.2 road miles: "an elegant yet comfortably renovated Chesterfield, NH farmhouse with its cathedral ceilings and rambling views of the Connecticut River Valley. Located in Southern New Hampshire on the Vermont border between Brattleboro, Vermont and Keene, New Hampshire." Its own navigation advertises pet-friendly rooms and Tesla and EV charging. Its room count is not published on the pages that could be reached, so this guide does not state one.

For food, Elm City Brewing Company is in The Colony Mill at 222 West Street, Keene, (603) 355-3335, 4.1 road miles from the course: "Opening in 1995, we are proud to be Keene's first brewery," and "Our soups, breads, sauces, salad dressings, and desserts are made fresh daily." Its published hours are Monday 11:30am to 9:00pm, closed Tuesday, Wednesday through Saturday 11:30am to 9:00pm and Sunday 11:30am to 8:00pm, and it states that it is "closed on New Years Day, Easter Sunday, Memorial Day, Independence Day, Labor Day, Thanksgiving, and Christmas Day." Lindy's Diner, 19 Gilbo Ave, (603) 352-4273, 3.9 road miles from the course, calls itself "A Paramount Diner Est. 1961," serves "Breakfast & Lunch all day," and publishes "–Closed all day on Tuesdays– All other days, including Sat & Sun: 6 am – 2 pm" — so Keene's brewery and its diner are dark on the same day of the week. The Chesterfield Inn's restaurant, at the inn's own address, is open to people not staying there: "We invite guests and the general public to come experience the great enthusiasm and creativity our chef brings to the kitchen," and "Dinner at our New Hampshire restaurant is served every night from 5:30 until 8:30 p.m., except Sunday." Reservations are suggested.

One warning about following local recommendations, including the inn's own. The Burrell House's page of things to do names two more Keene businesses, Luca's Mediterranean Café and Machina Kitchen & ArtBar, and neither is carried here, because no working operator page could be reached for either. The lucakeene.com address serves a 114-byte stub whose only content is a script redirecting to a parked lander. The machinaarts.org address redirects away entirely, to a site whose own title advertises an Indonesian online-gambling brand and whose 318 KB body contains the word "Keene" zero times and the word "Machina" zero times — a live, well-formed, HTTP 200 page that has nothing to do with the restaurant. This guide makes no claim about whether either business is trading; it only records that neither domain can be used as a source, and that a page returning 200 is not the same thing as a page about the place you looked up.

faq.question: How do I book a tee time on the North Course at Bretwood?
faq.answer: Through the operator's own general-public online portal, with no membership. Bretwood's tee-times page states that "Online tee time management is available for all guests," that "Active members can make tee time 14 days out. Non-members have 5 days," and that "Non-members can use the general public online tee time portal to book new tee times." That portal was driven directly: an unauthenticated request with no account was issued a session and returned Bretwood's own tee sheet, headed "Bretwood Golf Course — 365 East Surry Rd, New Hampshire, Keene, 03431 - United States," for four dates across the calendar, with a Login/Register control so an account can be made at the point of booking. There is no membership gate and no booking class. The one thing that test could not do is read a specific bookable time, because the slot list is drawn in the browser rather than sent by the server.

faq.question: Why is this guide not anchored on Golf Digest's New Hampshire ranking, the way most states in this set are?
faq.answer: Because the ranking has no publicly accessible entry to anchor on. It runs to exactly five courses — Baker Hill, The Golf Club of New England, Lake Winnipesaukee, Manchester Country Club and Lake Sunapee — and all five carry the label "Private" in their own header blocks, with five labels against five titles so none is missing or inherited. The word "Public" occurs zero times in the entire page, and zero times in six archived captures of it spanning March 2025 to May 2026, three of which are provably distinct snapshots by digest and hash. All five clubs also state a member-or-member's-guest gate on their own sites. With no "Public" entry at any rank, this guide uses the set's stated fallback: the publicly accessible course with the strongest verifiable competitive record, which is Bretwood's North Course.

faq.question: Isn't the Omni Mount Washington course the one to play in New Hampshire?
faq.answer: It is genuinely open to you — the resort's own FAQ answers "Do you have to be a guest staying at Omni Mount Washington Resort & Spa to play on the golf courses?" with "No, the public is welcome although resort guests have priority for booking tee times" — and it is a Donald Ross course completed in 1915, restored by Brian Silva and reopened on August 1, 2008. It is not this guide's course for one reason only, and it is a reason of record rather than access: the resort states the course "has hosted four New Hampshire Opens," which the championship's own venue history confirms as 1977, 1978, 1979 and 1980. Four against Bretwood's nineteen decides it. Separately, no green fee can be quoted for the Omni: its "Golf Rates And Fees" page publishes only a practice-range and rental table whose columns are Adult and Junior rather than guest and non-guest, with no green-fee figure and no dated qualifier anywhere on it.

faq.question: What does a round cost?
faq.answer: From Bretwood's own rate page, titled "Rates for 2026" and carrying the operator's date: "Rates listed here are current as of January 1, 2026. If a discrepancy exists, then the published rates in the Bretwood Golf Shop will take precedence over those found on this site." One card covers both courses. From opening day through Thursday May 31, 2026: 9 holes $34 Monday to Thursday and $38 Friday, weekend and holiday; 18 holes $52 and $58; 36 holes Monday to Thursday $105 including cart. After June 1, 2026: 9 holes $36 and $40; 18 holes $54 and $60; 36 holes Monday to Thursday $110 including cart, non holiday. A cart is $40.00 for two riders over 18 holes ($20.00 per person) or $25 for one rider; $24 for two or $15 for one over 9. Pull cart $4 and $8, club rental $10 and $20, range bucket $6 for 36 balls or $12 for 72.

faq.question: When is Bretwood open, and can I count on a given date?
faq.answer: The operator publishes a month range and nothing finer: "Open every day from April until mid-November (weather permitting)," and, on the membership page, "a season (April thru November)." Online tee times open "beginning April 1, Wednesday," with carts and tee times from 5:30 am on weekends and holidays and 6:00 am Monday through Friday. There is no season-dates page, no news page and no course-status page, so no exact opening or closing date is published and none is stated here. Nothing on the site indicates aeration, renovation or flood work — those words appear nowhere — and the only closure wording concerns the golf shop, not the course: "Tokens can be used after shop hours. Closed early Monday night for maintenance." The 2026 New Hampshire Open was played at Nashua Country Club, so no championship closed Bretwood that year.

faq.question: Which website is Bretwood's?
faq.answer: bretwoodgc.com. The similar-looking bretwoodgolf.com is not usable: over https it serves a 1,100-byte Squarespace parking page titled "Coming Soon" whose text reads "We're under construction," with no occurrence of "Bretwood" or "Keene" in it. Confusingly, the http form of that same address redirects to the real site, so whether the domain looks fine depends on which scheme you type. Use bretwoodgc.com.

faq.question: Can I play the South Course as well?
faq.answer: Yes, and the rate card is built for it — 36 holes Monday to Thursday is priced as a single day's golf at $105 before June 1, 2026 and $110 after, cart included. The South Course is on the same property at 0.0 road miles, on the same public booking portal and the same season statement. It is a full 18, not a short loop: its own published card reads 6,952 yards from the Gold tees, par 72, rated 73.5 with a slope of 132, with lateral water hazards along the Ashuelot River at holes 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 10, 11, 14 and 17.

faq.question: Where is the North Course, and where do I stay and eat?
faq.answer: At 365 East Surry Rd, Keene, NH 03431, in Cheshire County — the county exactly as the Census geocoder returns it for that address. Manchester–Boston Regional Airport (MHT) is 61.1 road miles away; Bradley International 85.8 and Boston Logan 92.8. In Keene, The Burrell House Inn at 112 Washington Street is 3.8 road miles from the course and has nine rooms; the Chesterfield Inn at 20 Cross Road, West Chesterfield, is 16.2 road miles and runs a dinner restaurant open to the general public every night except Sunday, 5:30 to 8:30 p.m. For food in town, Elm City Brewing Company at 222 West Street is 4.1 road miles away and Lindy's Diner at 19 Gilbo Ave is 3.9 — both closed on Tuesdays.

places.name: Bretwood Golf Course: North Course
places.summary: The fallback anchor for New Hampshire, chosen on competitive record because every one of the five entries on Golf Digest's 2025-'26 New Hampshire ranking is labelled "Private." Host of 19 New Hampshire Open Championships — more than any other course in the event's history, per New Hampshire Golf, and independently re-derived from the championship's venue-by-year table as 18 solo hostings plus the 2019 championship co-hosted with Keene Country Club. Architects Geoffrey Cornish and Hugh Barrett; 6,974 yards, par 72, rated 73.9 with a slope of 132 from the Gold tees, along the Ashuelot River with Penncross bentgrass greens. Half of a "36-hole public golf course (two 18 hole courses)" whose general-public booking portal was reached and driven without an account.

places.name: Bretwood Golf Course: South Course
places.summary: The second course at Bretwood, on the same property at 0.0 road miles from the North, sharing its clubhouse, rate card, season and public booking portal. A full, separate 18 rather than a practice loop, established three ways: the operator's "36-hole public golf course (two 18 hole courses)," the mapped course object's two 18-hole par-72 layouts named North and South, and its own complete published scorecard — 6,952 yards, par 72, rated 73.5 with a slope of 132 from the Gold tees. Local rules: "Out of Bounds: Behind green #12; Left of fairway #13," with lateral water hazards along the Ashuelot River at holes 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 10, 11, 14 and 17.

places.name: The Burrell House Inn
places.summary: 112 Washington Street, Keene, +1 (413) 239-9011 — 3.8 road miles from Bretwood and 0.3 road miles from Central Square. In its own words, "a historic New England family-owned boutique hotel that's newly renovated with modern amenities" with "9 beautifully restored rooms," each with private bath, wi-fi, smart TV, microwave, mini-fridge, coffee maker, coded entry and private parking. It does not serve breakfast and points guests to the town's restaurants and cafés instead.

places.name: Chesterfield Inn
places.summary: 20 Cross Road, West Chesterfield, (603) 256-3211 — 16.2 road miles from Bretwood. In its own words, "an elegant yet comfortably renovated Chesterfield, NH farmhouse with its cathedral ceilings and rambling views of the Connecticut River Valley. Located in Southern New Hampshire on the Vermont border between Brattleboro, Vermont and Keene, New Hampshire." Its own navigation advertises pet-friendly rooms and Tesla and EV charging. It runs a dinner restaurant open to the general public. No room count is published on the pages that could be reached, so none is stated.

places.name: Elm City Brewing Company
places.summary: The Colony Mill, 222 West Street, Keene, (603) 355-3335 — 4.1 road miles from Bretwood. "Opening in 1995, we are proud to be Keene's first brewery," and "Our soups, breads, sauces, salad dressings, and desserts are made fresh daily." Published hours: Monday 11:30am to 9:00pm; closed Tuesday; Wednesday through Saturday 11:30am to 9:00pm; Sunday 11:30am to 8:00pm. It states that it is closed on New Years Day, Easter Sunday, Memorial Day, Independence Day, Labor Day, Thanksgiving and Christmas Day.

places.name: Lindy's Diner
places.summary: 19 Gilbo Ave, Keene, (603) 352-4273 — 3.9 road miles from Bretwood. "A Paramount Diner Est. 1961," serving "Breakfast & Lunch all day." Its own published hours: "–Closed all day on Tuesdays– All other days, including Sat & Sun: 6 am – 2 pm." A working diner with new breakfast and lunch menus published on its site.

places.name: Chesterfield Inn Restaurant
places.summary: The dinner restaurant at the Chesterfield Inn, 20 Cross Road, West Chesterfield, open to people not staying there: "We invite guests and the general public to come experience the great enthusiasm and creativity our chef brings to the kitchen." In its own description, "seafood from Boston, herbs from our garden, and cheeses and produce from local farmers," with bread made fresh every day. "Dinner at our New Hampshire restaurant is served every night from 5:30 until 8:30 p.m., except Sunday." Reservations are suggested.

entries.name: Bretwood Golf Course: North Course
